chapter: Joining Earl Hines and the Grand Terrace
title: Joining Hines in place of Hayes Alvis and doubling
summary: He joined an established band on string bass and tuba and preferred tuba at first.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Let's go to Earl now. But you hadn't known him before he offered you the gig?
No.
The band was pretty well established back -- this is 1931?
Yeah.
So the band was pretty well established then?
Yeah.
Yeah. And you took Hayes Alvis's place?
Hayes Alvis, yeah.
Was Hayes playing just string bass, or did he also double, too?
What was he playing? Yeah, I know he was playing tuba, I don't know if he was playing string bass then or not.
Well, you went in on string bass?
I went in on string bass and tuba.
Doubling.
Doubling.
I hate to skip around like this, but was doubling common in those days --
Yeah.
You played both, you didn't play just one?
You played both. You played both, you didn't play just one.
Did you have a preference, which you liked to play?

At that time I liked the tuba better than the string bass, because string bass was kind of rough for me back in them days, you know. It takes years and years to perfect -- to get the perfection on the string bass, and then
And you don't have that on tuba?
Not necessarily. It's not as technical as string bass. Because most of the time you're oom-pahing on the tuba. Unless you take a solo or something, you know.
